searchText: There's another aspect to metrics which is that while some metrics can be universally implemented, others are tied to the specific implementation as well, and the optimizations and flow of data particular to the client - we've successfully had contributors port prysm dashboards to nimbus, and while it takes a little bit of effort, it's certainly reasonably doable - on one of the recent calls, there was a call to standardise some of the metrics at least, and a starting point might be https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-metrics - if someone wants to contribute, assessing what metrics clients share already and documenting similarities and difference would be a good starting point regarding slashing, slashings to date have been centered around people running multiple instances of the same validator - we have doppelganger protection as an (imperfect) guard against that in some clients - by the time you get to the metrics and long-term monitoring stage, you have already passed this most significant risk 😉 <@273808422753796097> https://ethresear.ch/t/adding-pos-validator-key-changes/9264 I really like this 😄 I believe this makes mev even more interesting, is there a waiting period delegating from one pool to another? I think a waiting period of 2 epochs would be ideal otherwise i’d switch to the pool that has the most block proposals in the next epoch (pool hopping) pplns protects against pool hopping on pow, not sure what the equivalent on pos would be > I think a waiting period of 2 epochs would be ideal otherwise i’d switch to the pool that has the most block proposals in the next epoch (pool hopping) > E You don't get the rewards of the pool you delegate to, you're just giving them the rights to control *your* validator i see, thanks I guess that depends on the pool, I wouldn't be very surprised if I see a large pool negotiating MEV off chain and then forcing their validators to use a pool owned coinbase to later split tx fees equally among all active validators in the pool at the time of the proposal. In such a scenario the weird phenomenon Butta alludes to would work thought the same, it makes more sense for pools to forward the rewards over N epochs and take a cut and potentially get even more block proposals in the next epoch.

excerpts.author: arnetheduck
excerpts.content: There's another aspect to metrics which is that while some metrics can be universally implemented, others are tied to the specific implementation as well, and the optimizations and flow of data particular to the client - we've successfully had contributors port prysm dashboards to nimbus, and while it takes a little bit of effort, it's certainly reasonably doable - on one of the recent calls, there was a call to standardise some of the metrics at least, and a starting point might be https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-metrics - if someone wants to contribute, assessing what metrics clients share already and documenting similarities and difference would be a good starting point

excerpts.author: arnetheduck
excerpts.content: regarding slashing, slashings to date have been centered around people running multiple instances of the same validator - we have doppelganger protection as an (imperfect) guard against that in some clients - by the time you get to the metrics and long-term monitoring stage, you have already passed this most significant risk 😉

excerpts.author: butta
excerpts.content:
<@273808422753796097> https://ethresear.ch/t/adding-pos-validator-key-changes/9264

I really like this 😄 I believe this makes mev even more interesting, is there a waiting period delegating from one pool to another? 
I think a waiting period of 2 epochs would be ideal otherwise i’d switch to the pool that has the most block proposals in the next epoch (pool hopping)

excerpts.author: butta
excerpts.content: pplns protects against pool hopping on pow, not sure what the equivalent on pos would be
